name: Localized Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Localized Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

criteria.description: Presence of localized blistering and scarring predominantly on trauma-prone areas
Skin biopsy showing sublamina densa cleavage with scarring
Identification of pathogenic variants in the COL7A1 gene
Reduced or absent type VII collagen at the dermoepidermal junction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, histopathology, and genetic testing) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by immunofluorescence mapping and family history.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized skin blistering following minor trauma
Atrophic scarring with milia formation in affected areas
searchTerms: thin, sunken scars with small white bumps

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nail dystrophy limited to affected regions

common.symptomName: Hyperkeratosis in areas of repeated trauma

occasional.symptomName: Mucosal involvement limited to oral cavity
Pseudosyndactyly in severely affected localized areas
searchTerms: fused fingers or toes in spots
skin causing finger or toe joining

occasional.symptomName: Hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation in scarred skin
searchTerms: lighter or darker skin in scars
patchy skin color changes in scars

rare.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma arising in chronic scars
searchTerms: skin cancer developing in old scars

rare.symptomName: Esophageal strictures due to mucosal involvement

laboratory: Immunofluorescence mapping demonstrating reduced or absent type VII collagen
imaging: High-resolution ultrasound may show skin layer separation in affected areas
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL7A1 gene encoding type VII collagen
other: Clinical observation of localized blistering and scarring pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering occurs intraepidermally rather than sublamina densa
Tense blisters with eosinophilic infiltrate on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly expanding blistering lesions with systemic symptoms
Signs of secondary infection or sepsis
Development of non-healing ulcers or suspicious lesions suggestive of malignancy
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2021.
Orphanet: Localized dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. ORPHA:595356.
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Matrix Biol. 2017.
